cues.en: And as a fundamentalist,
cues.zh: 作为一名原教旨主义者，

cues.en: I say, what's wrong with keyboards?
cues.zh: 我说，键盘到底有什么毛病？

cues.en: Why are they a bad idea from the point of view of information theory? Well, keyboards are inefficient, I'd say, for two reasons.
cues.zh: 从信息论的角度看，为什么它们是个坏主意？我觉得键盘效率低有两个原因。

cues.en: First,
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: keyboards don't take advantage of the predictability
cues.zh: 键盘并没有利用到这种可预测性

cues.en: of normal
cues.zh: 属于正常状态

cues.en: writing, if you're writing English, say.
cues.zh: 写作，如果你在写英文，那就说。

cues.en: Shannon's estimated that the actual information content of English, if you're generating it, is about one bit per character.
cues.zh: Shannon 估计，英语的实际信息量，如果是在生成它，大约是每字符一比特。

cues.en: In contrast, if you've got a 64 key keyboard like this one here, you press one of those 64 keys, each time you choose a key, you could have been conveying six bits of information, because two to the power six is 64. So there's a factor of six inefficiency there, because keyboards don't do language modeling.
cues.zh: 相比之下，如果你用的是像眼前这种64键键盘，每按下一个键，本来都能传递6比特的信息，因为2的6次方等于64。这就造成了6倍的效率浪费，因为键盘不做语言建模。

cues.en: Of course, were invented two hundred years ago before we had such things as language models.
cues.zh: 当然，键盘发明于两百年前，那时我们还没有语言模型这种东西。

cues.en: The second reason why keyboards are inefficient
cues.zh: 键盘低效的第二个原因

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 在于

cues.en: these things on the ends of my hands, we call them digits,
cues.zh: 我手上的这些部位，我们称之为手指（digits），

cues.en: but they're not actually digital devices. They're analogs. I've got 10 analogs, each one of them capable of high precision motor gestures with a lot of fine control. And keyboards throw all that away.
cues.zh: 但它们其实并不是数字设备（digital），而是模拟设备。我有10个模拟设备，每个都能做出高度精准、精细控制的动作手势。而键盘把这些优势全都浪费了。

cues.en: All you can do is detect whether a finger is up or down. And that's a big waste, again, of information content. It's been estimated that just a single finger
cues.zh: 它能做的只是检测手指是抬起还是落下。这同样是对信息量的巨大浪费。据估计，单凭一根手指

cues.en: can generate information at a rate of 14 bits per second.
cues.zh: 就能以每秒14比特的速率生成信息。

cues.en: So here is the sort of fantasy, the theoretical motivation for what we're doing in the Dasher project. Let's imagine solving both these problems. We're somehow going to have a language model in there so that
cues.zh: 所以这就是我们在 Dasher 项目中的某种构想和理论初衷。设想一下同时解决这两个问题：设法在系统中引入语言模型，使得

cues.en: the bits that a human generates are turned into characters efficiently.
cues.zh: 人类生成的比特能够高效地转化为字符。

cues.en: And we're going to get as many bits as possible out of a single muscle, maybe just one finger. And if we could plug one finger generating bits at a rate of 14 bits per second into a language model with a conversion rate of one bit per character, you would then be writing at 14 characters per second, which would correspond to 170
cues.zh: 同时，我们要从单块肌肉——比如仅凭一根手指——榨取出尽可能多的比特。如果能把这根以每秒14比特速率生成信息的手指，接入转换率为每比特一个字符的语言模型，打字速度就能达到每秒14个字符，相当于

cues.en: words per minute with just one finger. So that's the
cues.zh: 仅用一根手指就能达到每分钟170个词。这就是

cues.en: goal, the ultimate benchmark we'd like to achieve in this project.
cues.zh: 我们在该项目中想要达成的目标和终极基准。

cues.en: And how do we go about this? Well, steal from the best. And in information theory, they already know how to do text compression. And text compression is sort of an inverse process to writing. In text compression, you put in text, and out comes a bit string. And if it's a good compressor, the bit string is short.
cues.zh: 我们该怎么做呢？很简单，借鉴最好的。在信息论里，他们已经知道怎么做文本压缩了。文本压缩有点像是写作的逆过程。在文本压缩中，你输入文本，输出一个比特串。如果压缩算法好，这个比特串就会很短。

cues.en: Writing,
cues.zh: 而写作呢，

cues.en: you make some sort of gesture,
cues.zh: 你做一个手势，

cues.en: and out comes text. And an efficient writing system is a system where you make a brief gesture and out comes lots of text. So there's a sort of analogy here that writing is perhaps a bit like back to front text compression.
cues.zh: 然后输出文本。一个高效的写作系统，就是你做一个简单的手势，就能输出大量文本。所以这里有个类比，写作或许有点像反向的文本压缩。

cues.en: So let's steal from the very best. And the very best text compression method is an idea called arithmetic coding.
cues.zh: 那我们就借鉴最好的。最好的文本压缩方法是一个叫算术编码的想法。

cues.en: In arithmetic coding, you put in text and a probabilistic model for the language that you're writing in.
cues.zh: 在算术编码中，你输入文本以及你所写语言的概率模型。

cues.en: And out comes a binary string with a point in front of it, a binary point. You think of this binary string as defining a real number somewhere between zero and one. And the more bits get added, the higher the precision to which the real number has been defined.
cues.zh: 然后输出一个前面带点的二进制串，也就是二进制小数点。你可以把这个二进制串看作是定义了零和一之间的一个实数。添加的比特越多，对该实数定义的精度就越高。

cues.en: Arithmetic coding, if you don't know about it, I can recommend a textbook that describes it. It's available free online.

cues.zh: 编码了，因为 Dasher 本质上就是反向的算术编码。你输入一个手势，这是一个定义了实数、且精度越来越高的实值手势。你使用与最先进的文本压缩器完全相同的概率模型，然后就能输出文本。
